name: Freshchat
task: Website or Shopify chat & FAQ deflection
summary: AI-powered customer messaging from Freshworks: live chat and chatbots across your website, app, WhatsApp and Instagram, with a unified agent inbox and automation that deflects repetitive questions.
best_for: small-to-mid support teams that want live chat and messaging with a real free tier to start
skip_if: you need a full help-desk and ticketing system, not just chat — look at a complete support suite instead of bolting on channels
honest_knock: The free tier is genuinely useful for small teams, but AI features and higher-tier routing sit behind paid plans and add-ons — and being part of the wider Freshworks suite means you'll be nudged toward the full platform.

pricing.notes: Read 1 Sep 2026 and re-read 16 Oct 2026 on freshworks.com/live-chat-software/pricing/ (USD, both the Annually and Monthly views). Free is $0 for up to 10 agents. Per agent per month: Growth $19 billed annually or $23 monthly, Pro $49 or $59, Enterprise $79 or $95. Freddy AI is a separate bill, and both rates are published: the Freddy AI Copilot add-on is $29/agent/mo billed annually ($35 monthly), and Freddy AI Agent sessions cost $49 per 100 sessions beyond the 500 complimentary sessions each paid account receives once. Other add-ons on the same page: Freshcaller at $15/$39/$69 per agent per month annually ($18/$47/$83 monthly) on Growth/Pro/Enterprise, campaign contacts at $100, connector app tasks at $80, and day passes at $2/$7/$12.

sessions.what: The Freddy AI Agent in a Freshchat trial account, built in AI Agent Studio. We wrote a short help page for a made-up headset shop (shipping, returns, warranty, two products, opening hours: about 250 words) and gave the agent its URL as the only knowledge source; learning finished in about two minutes. We then ran 13 customer questions through the studio's Test screen: 10 whose answer is on the page, one that needs a small inference (shipping to Japan when the page lists only three countries) and two whose answer is not on the page at all (PayPal, and battery life with noise cancelling on). We scored every reply against the page.
findings: 11 of the 13 replies were correct, and every factual reply linked the help page as its source. That includes the trickier ones: an order at 4pm on a Tuesday ships on Wednesday because of the 15:00 cut-off, a cable broken by pulling is excluded from the warranty, and 'Do you ship to Japan?' got a clear no with the three countries we do ship to.

It did not invent anything where the page was silent. Asked about PayPal, it said the help centre has no information on payment methods. Asked for battery life with noise cancelling on, it gave the documented 40 hours, said that figure is with noise cancelling off, and declined to give a number for the other case.

The one wrong reply was 'Can I call you?'. The page says there is no phone support; the agent answered 'Sure! Assigning your chat to our support agent.' It treated the question as a request for a human and started a handover, and the 'Sure!' reads as a yes. The Test dashboard still counted this reply as Answered.
One reply added something the page does not contain: after correctly refusing the warranty claim, it offered to explain 'replacing the cable at your own cost', which our page never mentions.

The dashboard's totals (12 answered, 1 unanswered) are a useful first filter, but you have to read the replies: the handover counted as an answer, and the correct 'I don't know' about PayPal counted as unanswered.
not_tested: real chats through the website widget, other languages, larger or contradictory knowledge bases, and what the replies cost, because the Test screen is not live AI Agent sessions
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
